lines.say: Your app can get healthier by refusing requests. Sounds backwards.
lines.show: Your app can get healthier by refusing requests. Sounds backwards.

lines.say: Imagine one bot guessing passwords on your login page. Fifty thousand attempts in a minute.
lines.show: Imagine one bot guessing passwords on your login page. Fifty thousand attempts in a minute.

lines.say: After five tries, the gate closes. The next guess gets an error, not another chance.
lines.show: After five tries, the gate closes. The next guess gets an error, not another chance.

lines.say: That is rate limiting: a cap per user in a set time window.
lines.show: That is rate limiting: a cap per user in a set time window.

lines.say: Your server counts each user's requests separately. One noisy sender hits the limit while everyone else keeps using the app.
lines.show: Your server counts each user's requests separately. One noisy sender hits the limit while everyone else keeps using the app.

lines.say: Think of a bouncer with a clicker. Each guest gets five entries an hour. The sixth time, the door stays shut.
lines.show: Think of a bouncer with a clicker. Each guest gets five entries an hour. The sixth time, the door stays shut.

lines.say: Over the limit, the server answers with four twenty-nine: too many requests.
lines.show: Over the limit, the server answers with four twenty-nine: too many requests.

lines.say: Once that window passes, the count resets and they can try again.
lines.show: Once that window passes, the count resets and they can try again.

lines.say: So a runaway script cannot hog the app. Thousands of requests can be rejected to protect everyone else's work.
lines.show: So a runaway script cannot hog the app. Thousands of requests can be rejected to protect everyone else's work.

lines.say: The point is not to make every request succeed. It is to keep one sender from breaking the service for everyone.
lines.show: The point is not to make every request succeed. It is to keep one sender from breaking the service for everyone.
